findings.finding: With no front door and no allowedNamespaces the app NetworkPolicy has no ingress rule at all, and an empty ingress array denies every source (gcp/dispatch_kube.go:700-713), so the component would render a Dispatch nothing in the cluster can call — against the issue's Goal 'serves agent-token API calls in the cluster'.
findings.answer: Decision D1 and task T1.4: the resolver refuses an empty allowedNamespaces when the tailnet group is empty, naming the input. Proven by TestDispatchSandboxRefusesWhatItDoesNotBuild and TestDispatchSandboxAdmitsOnlyTheAllowedNamespaces (T3.6, T3.7).

findings.finding: Sign-in reaches a third place the issue does not name: the DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET key of Secret <hostname>-dispatch (gcp/dispatch_kube.go:345-346). Worse, refuseDispatchSeedInSecret calls value.ToStringOutput() (:256-262), so a nil pulumi.StringInput dereferences nil and crashes the provider — true of args.SignInClientSecret and of args.TailnetAuthKey at :338-339.
findings.answer: Task T2.1 and T2.2 gate both Secret call sites, not only the environment variables; Risk 1 records the crash. The sandbox Secret holds DATABASE_URL, DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN and DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY alone, asserted by TestDispatchSandboxRendersNoSignIn (T3.4), and TestConstructDispatchSandbox (T3.9) runs the plugin's own path where such a crash shows.

findings.finding: R1's 'the refusal names the missing ones' (one message listing all) would break four pre-existing rows of TestDispatchResolverRefusesInvalidInputs, which assert input-specific substrings (tags+'at least one', frontDoorToolsImage+'pinned by digest', signInDomain+'lowercase DNS name', tailnetDnsName+'ts.net'). A2 forbids changing those expectations.
findings.answer: Decision D4: a partial group keeps today's per-input refusal wording and each refusal of an unset input gains one clause naming every unset input of its group. That satisfies R1 literally and leaves every asserted substring in place. Proven by TestDispatchPartialTailnetGroupNamesEveryMissingInput (T3.8) with TestDispatchResolverRefusesInvalidInputs unedited.

findings.finding: 'The tailnet inputs' is six inputs including two images, and the four group combinations are undefined. The image loop (gcp/dispatch.go:681-690) checks all four images together, so an empty tailscaleImage fails imageRule today.
findings.answer: Task T1.3: the tailscaleImage and frontDoorToolsImage rows run only when the tailnet group is set; envoyImage and cloudSqlProxyImage are checked in both modes. Decision D3 settles the combinations: tailnet set + sign-in empty is allowed; tailnet empty + sign-in set is refused.

findings.finding: 'The in-cluster Service address' has no spelling, and url (gcp/dispatch.go:1222) and DISPATCH_SERVER_URL (gcp/dispatch_kube.go:575) are two separate code paths that could disagree. url is the component's contract with consumers outside this repository.
findings.answer: Decision D5 and tasks T1.5, T2.5, T2.6: one dispatchSettings.serverURL() derivation, as socks5Proxy() already is, giving http://<hostname>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8766 with no trailing slash. Proven by TestDispatchSandboxServesInTheCluster (T3.3), which asserts the output and the variable are the same string.

findings.finding: R2's 'the release notes name the first Dispatch image commit that carries this' cannot be produced: the envoy-infra release body is --generate-notes, and the image commit does not exist before the merge (release-envoy-listener.yaml builds ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/envoy:<full commit> from the main push). The hazard underneath is real: a sandbox stack pinning an envoyImage built before this change gets a pod that refuses to boot.
findings.answer: Decision D8: the changelog fragment and packages/envoy/infra/README.md state that sandbox mode needs an envoyImage built from a sjawhar/legion main commit at or after this change (T6), and the implementer's production check after the close records the merge commit and the image tag on the pull request.

findings.finding: A2's `gh release view envoy-infra-v<X.Y.Z>` is a post-merge fact handed to pre-merge phases: the release is automatic on the main push and is cut only when a commit carries a version-bumping conventional-commit type, so a chore:/docs: title silently fails R4.
findings.answer: Decision D9 and task T7.2: pre-merge the provable parts are the pull-request title beginning feat(envoy-infra): and the unchanged pre-existing tests and goldens; `gh release view` is a production-check row of the proof table.

findings.finding: R1-R4 cite dispatch://INFRA-243/spec 'Sandboxes', which carries no tailnet, sign-in, NATS, url or reachability requirement. The only supporting fact there is that root/, which holds the tailnet's admin objects, gets no sandbox stack. So 'no Google sign-in client' and 'in-cluster agent-token API only' are the architect's own decisions rather than the owner's.
findings.answer: Reported to the architect in the completion summary; it changes no task. The spec is approved at v3 and its design stands.

findings.finding: The spec's Problem names checkSignInSettings as a thing that refuses an empty sign-in set. It does not: it enters its refusal branch only when at least one sign-in setting is set (cmd/dispatch/signin.go:76-81). The single refusal is requireCookieSignIn.
findings.answer: Task T4.1: the boot change is one function and one call site; checkSignInSettings needs no edit, which keeps a partially configured production deployment refused. T4.3 keeps the second assertion of TestResolveBootConfigRefusesCookieIdentityWithoutTheWholeSignIn verbatim for that reason.

findings.finding: Documentation the no-deferral rule makes part of this change and the issue never names: packages/envoy/infra/README.md (the only place a consumer learns a mode exists, since the served schema carries no property descriptions), the five DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* settings rows whose Required text becomes false and from which the docs site's configuration reference is generated, cmd/dispatch/README.md, cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md, and the changelog fragments.
findings.answer: Task T6 names each file with its line ranges and the two fragment paths, and task T4.2 names the five settings rows (settings.go:50,52,54,56,58) with the shape check and the completeness test they must still pass.

findings.finding: frontDoorReplicas and frontDoorPdbMinAvailable are resolved and bounds-checked whatever the mode (gcp/dispatch.go:848) while the front door's budget is created inside a closure this mode never calls, so both would be accepted and silently ignored — the failure TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly exists to prevent.
findings.answer: Decision D2 and task T1.4: both are refused by name when the tailnet group is empty, in the clusterOnly precedent's shape, with a row each in TestDispatchSandboxRefusesWhatItDoesNotBuild (T3.7).

findings.finding: Proof surfaces: this pod has no Docker, no Postgres server, no pulumi CLI and no cluster write access (kubectl auth can-i create jobs|services both answer no), and storetest.Open skips without DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL, so the agent-token leg of A1 would skip silently.
findings.answer: The plan's proof table names a surface and a command per criterion, and its section 'The pod prerequisite for the two Postgres-backed rows' names the rootless Debian Postgres recipe (docs/solutions/testing/the-real-dispatch-stack-runs-inside-a-legion-pod-with-no-postgres-no-docker-and-no-root-INFRA-42.md), says pgvector is not needed here, and requires the --- PASS lines of each named test rather than a package-level ok (Risk 3).

findings.finding: R2's 'a refusal that says browser sign-in is off' may already be satisfied: /auth/start answers 503 SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED with a body naming the settings that would turn sign-in on. A reword would break an exact-string test and stale two documents.
findings.answer: Decision D6: the existing text satisfies R2; no wording change, and internal/dispatch/routes/router_test.go:785-800 stays unedited.

findings.finding: Residual safety of dropping requireCookieSignIn: a deployment that loses all five DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* values would boot with browser sign-in off instead of exiting 1. Candidate scope additions were a boot WARN and a /healthz field.
findings.answer: Decision D7: nothing is added. checkSignInSettings still refuses a partial set, so the common failure still refuses the boot, and /healthz already reports "signin": null (cmd/dispatch/main.go:1345-1349,1371-1377, asserted by issuer_down_test.go:56,78). STRATEGY.md: no protection against a failure nobody has seen.

findings.finding: A1's 'no tailnet resource is declared' needs the list: the registration golden holds nine front-door lines, and one of them, ConfigMap example-dispatch-serve, carries no 'tailnet' in its name, so a substring filter of the kind dispatch_cluster_only_test.go uses would keep it and pass while the sandbox still declared it.
findings.answer: Task T3.2: the sandbox expectation is the golden minus exactly nine lines named individually, the serve ConfigMap among them, compared with require.Equal over dispatchRegistrations(m).

findings.finding: Parts of R1 and R3 are already true at the base and must not be re-planned: the port-1055 Service, the front door's own NetworkPolicy and the DependsOn edges are all already gated on natsInCluster, and gcp:ClusteredNatsHub already runs with no tailnet.
findings.answer: The plan's 'Already true at 3d5548da' table records each with its file and lines, and no task repeats them.

specDepartures.spec: R1 and A1 list what the component must do when the tailnet inputs are empty and name no requirement on allowedNamespaces.
specDepartures.plan: The resolver refuses an empty allowedNamespaces whenever the tailnet group is empty, naming the input (decision D1, task T1.4), and the sandbox tests assert that refusal.
specDepartures.evidence: gcp/dispatch_kube.go:700-707 appends an allowedNamespaces rule only when that input is non-empty and then appends an unconditional rule admitting the front door's pods; :710-713 states that an ingress array with no rule denies every source. With no front door and no named namespace nothing in the cluster could reach Dispatch on 8766, so the Goal's 'serves agent-token API calls in the cluster' would be false.

outcome.scope: One refusal the spec does not name, needed for the Goal to hold. A sandbox consumer must name at least one namespace.

specDepartures.spec: R1 names the tailnet inputs the component must do without and says nothing about frontDoorReplicas or frontDoorPdbMinAvailable.
specDepartures.plan: Both are refused by name when the tailnet group is empty (decision D2, task T1.4), in the shape clusterOnly already uses.
specDepartures.evidence: gcp/dispatch.go:848 resolves and bounds both whatever the mode, and the front door's PodDisruptionBudget is created inside the deployment closure (gcp/dispatch_kube.go:466-474) that this mode never calls for <hostname>-tailnet, so both would be accepted and silently ignored. gcp/dispatch_cluster_only_test.go:194 exists so no input of this component is ignored in silence.

outcome.scope: Two refusals the spec does not name. No production deployment sets them without a front door.

specDepartures.spec: The Design says to make each tailnet and sign-in input optional and branch on emptiness, which reads as two independent groups; the spec refuses no combination of them.
specDepartures.plan: The sign-in group is refused when the tailnet group is empty (decision D3, task T1.4). The other mixed combination, tailnet set with sign-in empty, stays allowed.
specDepartures.evidence: DISPATCH_SERVER_URL is the sign-in callback origin (packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md:38-40), and with no tailnet it is http://<hostname>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8766, which no OAuth provider accepts as a redirect origin. The component would otherwise emit a configuration it knows cannot work. It also makes the spec's non-goal, people's browser sign-in in the sandbox, a rule.

outcome.scope: One refusal the spec does not name; it narrows the accepted input combinations by one that cannot work.

specDepartures.spec: R2: 'The release notes name the first Dispatch image commit that carries this.'
specDepartures.plan: The changelog fragment and packages/envoy/infra/README.md say sandbox mode needs an envoyImage built from a sjawhar/legion main commit at or after this change, and the implementer's production check after the close records the merge commit and the ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/envoy:<commit> tag on the pull request (decision D8, tasks T6 and T7).
specDepartures.evidence: The envoy-infra release body is GitHub's generated notes: .github/workflows/release-envoy-infra.yaml calls .github/scripts/release-push.sh release with no --notes, and that script defaults to --generate-notes, so no role can write a commit into it. The image commit does not exist before the merge: .github/workflows/release-envoy-listener.yaml builds ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/envoy with LEGION_COMMIT=${{ github.sha }} on the main push.

acceptance: R2's release-notes clause becomes a changelog and README statement plus the production check's record on the pull request.

specDepartures.spec: A2: 'gh release view envoy-infra-v<X.Y.Z> -R sjawhar/legion shows the release', listed among the criteria the tester and the reviewer judge.
specDepartures.plan: That command is a production-check row, run by the implementer after the close. Before the merge the release is proven by the pull-request title beginning feat(envoy-infra): (gh pr view --json title) and by the pre-existing tests and goldens passing unedited (decision D9, task T7.2).
specDepartures.evidence: release-envoy-infra.yaml runs on push to main with its build job gated on refs/heads/main, and .github/scripts/release-bump.sh bumps a version only for a feat, fix, refactor, perf or breaking subject, so no tag exists before the merge and none is cut at all for a chore: or docs: title.

acceptance: A2's gh release view moves from the pre-merge evidence to the production check, with the title check added in its place before the merge.
